audit.whatIsWrong: Four chart rows disagreed with their own whys and with the packet levelChart. Rows 1, 2 and 4 said Urgot while whys[1] ('skill fight'), whys[2] ('coin-flip') and whys[4] ('pull the all-in back to even') all say even; row 6 said Skill while whys[6] says Urgot out-paces his self-heal late.
audit.why: Volibear has Q, W and E by level 3 and his level-6 Stormbringer dive genuinely levels the all-in; Urgot's edge is level 4-5 and the Grievous Wounds item spike onward.
audit.corrected: phases[1]/win[1], phases[2]/win[2], phases[4]/win[4] set to Skill and phases[6]/win[6] set to Urgot, ratings adjusted, and the three full-layer whys rewritten so they no longer claim an Urgot win.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level-6 spike text described Stormbringer as making Volibear 'briefly untargetable-ish on landing' and 'gives a big shield'. Neither is in his kit.
audit.why: Stormbringer (R, 160/135/110s) leaps, slows and damages beneath him and grants bonus Health while disabling nearby enemy towers. The shield in his kit is Sky Splitter (E, 16s), granted when he stands in his own blast radius. There is no untargetability anywhere in the kit.
audit.corrected: spikes[1].text and content.mid now say bonus health plus tower disable, name Sky Splitter as the actual shield, and carry the 160s rank-1 R cooldown.
sources: enemyKit R (bonus Health, tower disable, cd 160/135/110)

audit.whatIsWrong: Volibear's on-hit profile was never stated, so the page reads the trade as pure armour maths. dosFull[2].d and dontsFull[1].d were generic filler under titles about poke and his heal.
audit.why: Frenzied Maul (W, flat 5s cooldown) applies on-hit effects and heals him on the second cast into the same target; The Relentless Storm stacks attack speed and eventually adds magic damage to nearby enemies. Attack speed plus a 5s heal means extended trades favour him, and armour alone misprices the exchange.
audit.corrected: dosFull[2].d now states the on-hit and attack-speed stacking with the Steelcaps answer; dontsFull[1].d carries Frenzied Maul's 5s cooldown and the keep-it-short rule. Thundering Smash's 12s rank-1 stun cooldown is now in phases[2].why.

edits.before: E or W second depending on kill pressure. A landed E-flip into W spray already wins most level-2 exchanges outright.
edits.after: E or W second depending on kill pressure. Short trades still hinge on who lands their combo — Frenzied Maul heals him back.

edits.before: Full legs rotation online — this is your lane now. Walk Volibear down with W whenever Thundering Smash (Stun) is on cooldown.
edits.after: Full legs rotation online, but he has Q, W and E too — Thundering Smash stuns off an auto, so trade only once it is down 12s.

edits.before: Fear Beyond Death online — at 25% HP Volibear is simply dead. Trade him to half, then the chain threat decides everything.
edits.after: Fear Beyond Death online, but Stormbringer answers it — his leap adds bonus health and disables your tower, so the 6 spike is even.

edits.before: Sterak's + Cleaver makes your W-trades unloseable head-on. Volibear must dodge E forever or find a jungler — punish the first mistake with R.
edits.after: Sterak's + Cleaver plus Grievous Wounds out-paces Frenzied Maul's self-heal — meet his dive with W-lock and E-flip and take the long fight.

edits.before: Volibear R (Stormbringer) makes him briefly untargetable-ish on landing, disables a turret and gives a big shield — respect his all-in dive, and hold your own R to execute him after his shield burns down.
edits.after: Volibear R (Stormbringer) is a 160s leap that grants him bonus health and disables your turret — the shield is Sky Splitter (E), so respect the dive, then execute him once that bonus health has been chewed off.

edits.before: At level 4 you start to pull ahead as your full Q-W-E kit lets you slow, shred and flip his engage; but level 6 swings it back to a coin-flip because Stormbringer gives him a shield, a tower disable and a strong dive. Hold your R to punish him after that shield expires rather than throwing it into the shield.
edits.after: At level 4 you start to pull ahead as your full Q-W-E kit lets you slow, shred and flip his engage; but level 6 swings it back to a coin-flip because Stormbringer leaps in for bonus health, disables your turret and lets him dive. Hold your R until that bonus health and his Sky Splitter shield are both gone.

edits.before: Volibear wastes Thundering Smash (Stun) — commit the full pattern immediately.
edits.after: Frenzied Maul applies on-hit and his passive stacks attack speed — Steelcaps.

edits.before: Burning your answer for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Frenzied Maul is a 5s cooldown — long trades feed his heal, so keep it short.

notes: The 'untargetable-ish' claim about Stormbringer was the worst error here — nothing in Volibear's kit grants untargetability, and it would have taught the player to hold R for a window that does not exist. Whether Urgot's E-flip can interrupt Thundering Smash's charge, and whether tenacity shortens its stun meaningfully, are not in Riot's text and I asserted neither.
